entries.title: Jeremiah 17:1
segments:
Upon the horns of your altars; your idolatrous altars.  The allusion is to the blood of their idol-offerings, sprinkled upon the horns of their altars, which was a fit symbol of their inveterate inward love of idolatry. 
 
vv 1-2. 
 
So deep and indelible is the handwriting of sin upon the human soul, that nothing can efface it but the power of divine grace.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:2
segments: Groves; rather, "images of Astarte," a female deity.  These, as well as their idolatrous altars, were erected on high hills and under green trees.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:3
segments: My mountain in the field; Jerusalem, probably so called because it stands on a mountain, with valleys on either side and a plain on the south-west.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:4
segments: Even thyself; literally, "even in thyself," that is, through thine own fault.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:5
segments:
vv 5-6. 
 
The original and universal sin of the human heart is departing from God and making flesh its confidence.  This idolatry of earthly things is the source of the wickedness and misery with which the earth is filled.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:6
segments: Shall not see when good cometh; shall have no share in it.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:7
segments:
vv 7-8. 
 
They who put their trust in the living God, continually receive from him light and life and prosperity.  The heavenly joy and peace which fill their souls keep them in the way of holiness, and prevent them from turning aside after the sinful delights of the wicked.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:8
segments: Shall not see when heat cometh; shall not feel its withering power.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:9
segments:
vv 9-10. 
 
A deep and habitual distrust of ourselves, with earnest prayer to God to show us what is in our hearts, and keep us from being deluded and destroyed by their desperate deceitfulness and wickedness--this is the beginning of all true wisdom and safety.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:11
segments:
Sitteth on eggs, and hatcheth them not; rather, "gathereth" eggs "which she hath not laid:" thus she loses her labor; for the young birds, when hatched, forsake her. 
 
Unjust gain does not profit its owner: he must soon part with it, and go to receive the reward of his folly and wickedness.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:13
segments: Written in the earth; in the dust of the grave; that is, be enrolled as its inhabitants.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:14
segments: Heal me, O Lord; here begins the prophet's prayer against his persecutors.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:16
segments:
Hastened; eagerly withdrawn myself. 
 
  From being a pastor to follow thee; literally, "from being a pastor after thee;" that is, from performing the duties of a prophet in obedience to thee.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:18
segments: God will consider the persecution which his faithful servants receive for the truth's sake as an injury done to himself; and if it be not repented of, will punish it accordingly.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:19
segments: The Sabbath is an indispensable bulwark of religion and good morals. Every nation that habitually profanes it must speedily sink into corruption, and become a vessel of wrath fitted for destruction.

entries.title: Jeremiah 17:26
segments: The plain; the low country along the Mediterranean, from Joppa to Gaza.  The meaning of these enumerations is, that they shall come from all parts of the land.
